name: Question 1
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-10\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t)\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{t}^{5}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-10.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-10 & =\frac{1}{10}(0)^{5}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}+C \\ -10 & =0+C \\ C & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{10}{t}^{5}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-10.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{1}{10}(2)^{5}-\frac{3}{4}(2)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}-10 \\  & =3.2-12+2-10 \\  & =-16.8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $16.8\,\text{m/s}.$

Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=12t4−3t3+t, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=−10m/s when t=0s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=2s.

a
10.8m/s
b
16.8m/s
c
−16.8m/s
d
7.2m/s
e
−10.8m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(12t4−3t3+t)dt=110t5−34t4+12t2+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=−10. Substituting this into the above gives

−10=110(0)5−34(0)4+12(0)2+C−10=0+CC=−10.

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=110t5−34t4+12t2−10.

We evaluate the velocity at time t=2s:

v(2)=110(2)5−34(2)4+12(2)2−10=3.2−12+2−10=−16.8m/s

Finally, since the speed is equal to |v(t)|, we conclude that the speed of the particle is 16.8m/s.
